DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

A Statue That Watches Itself

STS-HS12-L4-1400P-HSVPAMA1112-BNB-CFI-01 • HS Media Arts 11–12 • Audience Experience, Intention, and Persuasion in Media Artworks
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
In 1974, just before his New York gallery show opened, the Korean-born artist Nam June Paik found an empty wall. He placed an old Buddha statue in front of a TV and aimed a live camera at it, so the statue watched itself on the screen. Critics saw an ancient Asian tradition meeting modern Western television, fused into a new art form called video art, and today this class is reporting live from its own version.
Why do you think Paik made the statue, and not the audience, the one watching the screen?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Mateo doing?
Look at the picture. Build a reasoned spoken answer about Mateo's action, grounded in visible evidence, and connect it to how the class is staging the exhibit.
2
What is Amani holding?
Look at the picture. Build a reasoned spoken answer about what Amani holds, and evaluate how a live broadcast persuades its audience to pay attention.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Build a reasoned spoken answer about the teacher's action, and analyze how her control of the wall manages the audience's experience.
4
What place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Build a reasoned spoken answer about this place, weigh the competing clues, and explain why this setting suits a live report on video art.
5
Tell me about this artwork.
Look at the picture. Build a reasoned spoken answer about this artwork, and argue how its closed loop shapes the meaning a viewer takes away.
6
What is Jiwoo wearing?
Look at the picture. Build a reasoned spoken answer about Jiwoo's clothing, and argue how it echoes the fusion of traditions in the artwork.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: CA Arts Standards, Media Arts Re7b — Analyze how a variety of media artworks manage audience experience, create intentionality and persuasion, and convey purpose, meaning, and intent. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
